cases.why: (null - 5) is NaN, and a comparator that returns NaN leaves rows in whatever order the engine started with -- the table looks sorted and is not, which is worse than refusing to sort
the Playoff Odds header loses its sort key, so the column renders and refuses to sort -- the exact half-working state that joining the value onto the team object exists to prevent
an unsimulated team renders as though it had odds, so 'we never ran this team' and a real percentage become indistinguishable on the page
the colspan lags the column count, so the 'no teams' row draws a ragged edge exactly when something has gone wrong and the reader most needs the page to look deliberate
the column ships as a bare percentage, which reads as 'the model is 67.5% sure' rather than 'the team made the playoffs in 67.5% of 10,000 simulated seasons' -- a different and much stronger claim
the # is recomputed from the row's position, so sorting by Playoff Odds prints '#1' beside the ninth-rated team on a page called Power Ratings -- and '#1' is the part a casual reader carries away

the '#' header starts sorting, which this suite's header/field check explicitly exempts it from -- the exemption is only sound while the early return exists, so losing it silently widens what that guard permits

the Team Deep-Dive bar still encodes a signed net rating from the middle of the track but stops drawing the zero, so a small positive and a small negative render as the same short mark near the centre and are distinguishable only by reading the number beside them
